About the World Health & Disparities event

World Health & Disparities is a Health Science event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA World Health & Disparities 2026–27 test plan, built on the event’s official web references: WHO Health Equity, NIMHD, KFF and Our World in Data. Statistics are quoted with their source and year so you can verify them; invented teaching datasets are labeled as invented. Lessons include population-rate laboratories, evidence benches, case simulations and sorting activities. Read the assigned Barr text alongside this course.

Sample World Health & Disparities questions

1. Why is climate change considered a health equity issue?

  1. It affects every person exactly equally
  2. It only affects wealthy countries
  3. It has no proven link to health
  4. Its harms fall hardest on the poorest
Show answer

D. Its harms fall hardest on the poorest

Heat, floods and food insecurity disproportionately affect low-income communities and countries.

2. Why do researchers call for disaggregated data?

  1. Combined data are always more accurate
  2. Disaggregation reduces sample sizes for no reason
  3. Broad categories can hide large differences among subgroups
  4. It removes the need for any surveys
Show answer

C. Broad categories can hide large differences among subgroups

Outcomes differ greatly among Asian American subgroups and among Hispanic subgroups, for example.

3. What does health literacy mean?

  1. Finding, understanding and using health information
  2. The number of years of school completed
  3. The ability to read medical journals
  4. Knowing the names of all common diseases
Show answer

A. Finding, understanding and using health information

Limited health literacy occurs at every education level and is linked to poorer outcomes.
